purpose: Licensed SFX candidates for the 120 s film: 100 short sounds in 14 categories, every one measured numerically (not listened to).

method.analysis: Each file was decoded with ffmpeg (float, 44.1 kHz, native channels) in the Higgsfield sandbox and measured on the exact trimmed slice given in trim (trim = seconds inside the source file; reverse:true means reverse that slice). peak_dbfs = max |sample| over all channels; rms_dbfs = RMS over the active part (>-45 dB below the slice peak); centroid_hz = spectral centroid; clipping_pct = share of samples with |x|>=0.999; low_energy_lt120hz = share of spectral energy below 120 Hz (sub weight); attack_s = time from -30 dB below peak to the peak; rise_db = mean level of the last third minus the first third of the slice (positive = builds, negative = decays, ~0 = steady bed).
method.selection: Chosen by name/metadata and numbers only; nobody listened. Rejected: clipping >0.1%, long silence, or licences that are NC/ND/SA/unverifiable. Peaks decoded above 0 dBFS are flagged in notes (lower gain in the mix).
method.refetch: Every sound has a direct url (HTTP 200 when downloaded), file_in_pack (member path inside the zip/7z, or the file itself) and trim, so any file can be re-fetched and re-cut by script. Kenney files are only distributed as zips (url = the pack zip).

Mixkit: raw files must not be redistributed (do not commit them to a public repo); licence read from a Wayback capture; User Terms unread.
Six CC BY 4.0 Commons files (Work With Sounds) need the credit strings in credits_required.
MachinePowerOff, the-shop fridge drone and the MP3/24-32-bit sources have different sample rates/bit depths (see format); resample when rendering.
